title: Cohort-based Canary Evaluations with Autonomous Rollback Controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a cohort-driven A/B and canary evaluation pipeline that automatically detects quality regressions (semantic accuracy, hallucination rate, safety failure rate) and triggers an autonomous rollback controller when thresholds are exceeded. This ticket covers design and implementation of: cohort assignment logic, sample-size gating, statistical test selection (Wilson/bootstrapped CI), multi-metric decision rules, a rollout-controller endpoint that can revert model/config rollouts, and integration with Console dashboards, Grafana alerts, Slack notifications, and the oncall runbook. The system must support staged ramp percentages (e.g., 5/20/50/100) and allow manual overrides. Key goals: minimize false rollbacks while ensuring high-confidence protection against regressions that impact customers or SLOs.

acceptance_criteria: Cohort assignment implemented and deterministic for given user/session id across retries and releases.
Pipeline computes per-cohort metrics in real-time (1 minute aggregation windows) and evaluates statistical significance using configured tests.
Rollout-controller can revert a deployment to previous model/config within the configured rollback window and emits a detailed rollback event to Console.
Automatic rollback triggers combine multiple metrics: answer_accuracy absolute drop >= 3% AND p-value <= 0.01 OR hallucination_rate delta >= 2% absolute, with a minimum sample-size of 500 per cohort.
Console dashboard shows side-by-side metric diffs for canary vs baseline, with links to raw evaluation examples and offending prompts.
Notifications are sent to Slack and PagerDuty and the runbook is started automatically on rollback; manual abort/confirm endpoints exist.
Integration tests cover race conditions for overlapping rollouts and ensure backoff prevents flip-flop rollbacks.
implementation_notes: Use local streaming aggregator (kafka consumer) to compute rolling windows of metrics and push deltas to metrics-store with cohort tags.
Leverage existing eval-harness for the synthetic prompt set and add an embedding-based similarity check for hallucination detection (cosine < 0.7 flagged).
Rollout-controller exposes POST /rollback with authentication and audit logging. It calls deployment-service revert API and writes an event to the Console event stream.
Add feature flag to enable autonomous rollbacks per-organization with a safe default of manual-only for new customers.
Expose thresholds and decision rules as JSON policy in the Console with a validation UI and preflight simulator that runs the last 24h of traffic.
Consider future extension: adaptive thresholds that account for baseline variability per-customer and model type.
